name: Zoning-and-Rent-Burdens
what_it_holds: Python/R pipeline combining Census ACS data (via API), 2021 TIGER/Line shapefiles (CBSA + state boundaries), HUD Fair Market Rent + CHAS data (via HUD API), and the Wharton Residential Land Use Regulatory Index (WRLURI, dated 2020-01-15) to study how metro zoning stringency affects rent burden. No large data files committed (pulls live via API keys stored in apitext.txt/hudapitext.txt); generates merged CSVs at run time via census_data.py / hud_data.py / cleaning_data.py.
why_useful: WRLURI + ACS rent-burden combination is a genuinely distinct angle (housing-supply elasticity by metro) that could help explain why some ABNB markets see faster STR-to-LTR conversion pressure than others; more research-package than raw feed but the WRLURI linkage is uncommon in this space.
time_coverage: WRLURI vintage (2018 index) + ACS multi-year estimates
themes: Long-term rent indices: Zillow ZORI/ZHVI downloaders, Apartment List, Redfin data center, Realtor.com, HUD Fair Market Rents, Census ACS rent, CoStar-like
Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
why_all: WRLURI + ACS rent-burden combination is a genuinely distinct angle (housing-supply elasticity by metro) that could help explain why some ABNB markets see faster STR-to-LTR conversion pressure than others; more research-package than raw feed but the WRLURI linkage is uncommon in this space.
Links zoning/regulatory restrictiveness to rent burden — a possible proxy for STR-adjacent housing-supply constraint by metro, tangential to gap 13 and gap 12 (regulation).

Working, reusable example of pulling HUD FMR + CHAS + WRLURI + Census ACS together at metro/county level -- a template for the host-supply-economics / STR<->LTR crossover gap (#13). Confirms HUD API + WRLURI are machine-pullable; not itself a new dataset.

name: mcp-fairrent
what_it_holds: MCP server wrapping HUD housing data APIs: Fair Market Rents (FMR), Section 8 income limits, and a USPS ZIP-to-jurisdiction crosswalk. TypeScript, 0 stars, last updated 12 Sep 2026 (2 days before this scout).
why_useful: A structured, queryable client for HUD FMR/income-limit data that an agent (or our pipeline) could call directly instead of hand-parsing HUD CSVs; very fresh.
themes: Long-term rent indices: Zillow ZORI/ZHVI downloaders, Apartment List, Redfin data center, Realtor.com, HUD Fair Market Rents, Census ACS rent, CoStar-like
Rental listing scrapers and datasets (Craigslist, Zillow rentals, Apartments.com, Idealista, Rightmove, Zoopla, Immoscout24, SeLoger, Immobiliare, Domain, realestate.com.au)
why_all: A structured, queryable client for HUD FMR/income-limit data that an agent (or our pipeline) could call directly instead of hand-parsing HUD CSVs; very fresh.

Directly matches CONTEXT.md gap 13's explicit call-out of 'HUD FMR' -- a live, current, one-call method to pull official US fair-market-rent benchmarks by ZIP/jurisdiction, useful for host-supply-economics and regional cost-of-living cross-checks. Government source (HUD), not scraped -- no ToS concern.

name: mortgagerate-api
what_it_holds: Client/wrapper for retrieving current and historical US 30-year and 15-year fixed mortgage rates from Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey (weekly averages). Pushed 16 Jul 2026.
why_useful: Mortgage rates are a lever on host supply economics (buy-vs-rent-out decision, refinancing pressure on STR hosts) named explicitly in gap 13; this is a clean historical weekly series access method.
